newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TIGER TURNED AWAY AFTER TRYING TO GET EARLY PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER TURNED AWAY AFTER TRYING TO GET EARLY PRACTICE.

text.p: The early bird catches the worm, as the saying goes, but golfing early bird Tiger Woods caught some flack on Wednesday for trying to get a head start on practice for the U.S. Open.

Woods tried to duck onto the back nine of the Congressional Country Club course before 7 a.m. to enjoy an uncluttered, solitary practice tour before the masses of players and fans found their way to the course.
The 21-year-old Masters champion got as far as the 12th hole before officials asked him to leave and give course groundskeepers a chance to complete their mowing work on the greens and fairways.
Other players were also turned away, including Ian Woosnam and Davis Love.
Love said later he was amazed at all the activity he encountered at such an early hour at the course.

"We were out on the 10th hole at 7:15 and I'm not exaggerating there were 40 people working on the 10th hole -- mowing fairways, rolling the greens and blowing the fringes and raking bunkers," Love said.
"They're doing every little thing they can to make it perfect," he said, showing no rancour at being asked to join the queue teeing off from the first tee. "It's a treat to play it."
